es.summary: El cálculo preciso de la dosis asegura que el paciente reciba la cantidad adecuada del fármaco, evitando subdosificación o sobredosis.
key_points: Convertir siempre a unidades métricas (kg, mg, mL).
Usar la fórmula Dosis = (Orden × Peso) ÷ Concentración.
Verificar la frecuencia y dividir la dosis total diaria según lo indicado.
Revisar la orden, la etiqueta del medicamento y la identificación del paciente antes de administrar.
Documentar la dosis calculada y la verificación doble por otro profesional.
Conocer los rangos terapéuticos y ajustar según niveles séricos cuando sea necesario.

nursing_care: Obtener peso del paciente y convertir a kg (1 kg = 2.2 lb).
Leer la orden y la concentración del fármaco (mg/ mL).
Aplicar la fórmula y redondear según la presentación disponible.
Realizar doble verificación con otro enfermero o farmacéutico.
Retener la medicación si la dosis calculada supera el rango terapéutico y notificar al médico.
Registrar la dosis administrada, cálculo y verificación en la hoja de enfermería.
patient_teaching: Explicar al paciente la importancia de la dosis exacta y los posibles efectos de una sobredosis.
Instruir al paciente a reportar cualquier efecto inesperado después de la administración.
Reforzar la necesidad de informar cambios de peso que puedan afectar la dosificación.

outcomes: Seguridad del paciente: sin eventos de sobredosis durante la hospitalización.
Exactitud de la administración: 100% de dosis calculadas correctamente.

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar el peso actual del paciente en kg.
interventions.rationale: El peso es esencial para calcular dosis basadas en mg/kg.

interventions.action: Convertir todas las unidades a métricas antes de calcular.
interventions.rationale: Previene errores de conversión que pueden alterar la dosis.

interventions.action: Aplicar la fórmula de cálculo de dosis y redondear según la presentación disponible.
interventions.rationale: Asegura que la dosis sea administrable y segura.

interventions.action: Realizar doble verificación del cálculo con otro profesional de salud.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la probabilidad de errores de cálculo.

interventions.action: Comparar la dosis calculada con los rangos terapéuticos recomendados.
Documentar detalladamente el proceso de cálculo y la verificación.
interventions.rationale: Proporciona trazabilidad y evidencia de la práctica segura.

en.summary: Accurate dose calculation ensures the patient receives the appropriate amount of medication, preventing underdosing or overdose.
key_points: Always convert to metric units (kg, mg, mL).
Use the formula Dose = (Order × Weight) ÷ Concentration.
Verify frequency and divide the total daily dose as indicated.
Check the order, medication label, and patient identification before administration.
Document the calculated dose and double-check by another professional.
Know therapeutic ranges and adjust based on serum levels when necessary.

nursing_care: Obtain the patient’s weight and convert to kg (1 kg = 2.2 lb).
Read the order and medication concentration (mg/mL).
Apply the formula and round according to the available presentation.
Perform double verification with another nurse or pharmacist.
Hold the medication if the calculated dose exceeds the therapeutic range and notify the physician.
Record the administered dose, calculation, and verification on the nursing chart.
patient_teaching: Explain to the patient the importance of the exact dose and potential effects of an overdose.
Instruct the patient to report any unexpected effects after administration.
Emphasize the need to inform about weight changes that may affect dosing.

outcomes: Patient safety: no overdose events during hospitalization.
Accuracy of administration: 100% of doses calculated correctly.

interventions.action: Obtain and record the patient’s current weight in kg.
interventions.rationale: Weight is essential for calculating mg/kg doses.

interventions.action: Convert all units to metric before calculating.
interventions.rationale: Prevents conversion errors that can alter the dose.

interventions.action: Apply the dose calculation formula and round according to the available presentation.
interventions.rationale: Ensures the dose is administrable and safe.

interventions.action: Perform double verification of the calculation with another health professional.
interventions.rationale: Reduces the likelihood of calculation errors.

interventions.action: Compare the calculated dose with recommended therapeutic ranges.
Document the calculation and verification process in detail.
interventions.rationale: Provides traceability and evidence of safe practice.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Epilepsy and Anticonvulsant Drugs

summary.0.quote: Medication calculations are an important skill for the nurse to perform correctly to ensure the patient receives the right dose.

key_points.0.quote: This calculation may involve converting a metric system measurement into a household measurement or a household measurement into an apothecary measurement.

key_points.1.quote: The formula method , sometimes referred to as the “desired over have method,” divides the desired amount by the amount on hand, then multiplies it by the quantity on hand to determine the dose.

key_points.2.quote: Step 3: Divide the dose by the frequency 1,200 mg/day / 2 (BID) = 600 mg/dose

key_points.5.quote: Careful review of serum blood levels—trough levels and peak levels—is crucial to make appropriate dosing adjustments.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: The desired amount ( D ) is the dose prescribed, the amount on hand ( H ) is the available dose or concentration, and the quantity ( Q ) is the form and amount in which the drug is supplied.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: When it is possible to administer a fraction of a dose, medications are typically rounded to the nearest tenth for adults and to the nearest hundredth for children, unless otherwise indicated by the agency’s policy.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: If ever in doubt, ask a colleague to double-check the calculation to ensure the dose is accurate.
